paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God doesn't just point at a destination. He goes with His people the whole way there. He says, "Behold, I am sending an angel before you to protect you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared." (Exodus 23:20) The road, the protection and the place at the end all belong to Him.

But that promise comes with a call to listen. God says, "Pay attention to him and listen to his voice," and He says that if they listen carefully and do everything He says, He will be an enemy to their enemies. (Exodus 23:21-22) Then He says the same thing about their worship: "So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He will bless your bread and your water." (Exodus 23:25) And He warns that serving other gods "will surely be a snare" to them. (Exodus 23:33) You know that one thing you tell yourself is no big deal, and then it's EVERYTHING? That's the snare, friend.

He also tells them He will drive the nations out "little by little." (Exodus 23:30) That means the promise is big, but the walk is slow, and the slow part is still part of His plan. So when your own road feels slow, you can keep listening and keep serving, because He's the One going ahead of you. And the story isn't over, because the covenant at Sinai still has more ahead.
